paragraphs.en: Each player begins with 1–5 dice, normally five. Only you see your cup. A bid states how many dice of one face exist under all cups together. Raise the bid or challenge it. A false bid costs its bidder a die; challenging a true bid costs the challenger a die. A bid is true when at least the stated count exists. Players with no dice are eliminated. The last player with dice wins.

Classic uses no wilds. Raise the quantity, choosing any face, or keep the quantity and raise the face. Red Dead style adds Exactly: if the count is exact, every other player loses a die; otherwise the caller loses one. Perudo counts ones as wilds for other faces. A normal Perudo round cannot open on ones. Changing to ones requires half the last quantity rounded up; changing from ones requires double plus one. Increasing a bid of ones requires more ones.

Optional Perudo Palifico applies for one round when its starter first falls to one die and more than two players remain. Ones stop being wild; faces cannot change except for players who have already declared Palifico. Optional Calza lets anyone except the bidder claim an exact count before the next accepted bid. A correct Calza recovers one die up to the starting limit; an incorrect one loses a die. After a loss, the loser or next surviving seat starts. After successful Red Dead Exactly, the caller starts. After successful Calza, the last loser starts.

Players first save secret commitments; the server then supplies a new random seed. Together these determine the hidden dice. Secrets are revealed and verified only after a challenge. Bots use their own cup and public bids. Keep the same Elten profile to retain your secrets. Saving or transferring a pending secret is blocked; an unrelated participant can still be replaced.

Arrows and Enter choose a minimum legal bid for a face or a challenge. B opens a form for your own quantity and face. K calls bluff, D calls exactly when available. V reads your dice, L reads the current bid. Rolls and reveals happen through the shared executor automatically. F1 lists shortcuts; Ctrl+F1 opens rules. Chat, history and volume use shared controls.
